title: Crestwood strategy checkpoint: EU onramp and billing pathway
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer readiness to extend contract for 12 months with a 25% committed capacity uplift and to onboard an EU region. Discussed options for Dedicated vs Private VPC for data residency, latency targets, billing/pricing pathways, and next steps for security docs and a short benchmark pilot.
topics: Private VPC pilot vs Dedicated capacity
Benchmark plan and SOW next steps
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing & 12-month amendment draft (Alyssa) - by 2027-06-15
SE to run 48-hr benchmark plan doc + test matrix (Marco) - deliver by 2027-06-18
Send security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, KMS integration notes) and SAML doc (Jules) - by 2027-06-11
Schedule hands-on pilot kickoff (customer + infra) - target week of 2027-06-21
action_items: Alyssa Chen - Prepare amendment draft with 25% committed capacity uplift and pricing scenarios - 2027-06-15
Marco Ruiz - Produce benchmark plan (200rps target, 90th pct latency targets) and tooling list - 2027-06-18
Jules Park - Share security/compliance pack, SOC2 report, KMS/HSM notes, SAML setup guide - 2027-06-11
Eileen Cho (Crestwood) - Provide current traffic profile and peak hours CSV for batching recommendations - 2027-06-12
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-06-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Alyssa, Marco, Jules (Redwood) / Dana, Priya, Eileen, Samir (Crestwood)

00:00 Alyssa Chen: OK hi everyone thanks for joining, we're on for the Crestwood strategy checkpoint. small agenda — term, capacity, EU onramp, security, pilot. sound right?
00:14 Dana Ortega: Yup, that's perfect. we have about 45 minutes of content then we'll do Qs. trying to move fast because procurement has a window.
00:28 Marco Ruiz: quick note — i'll focus on the benchmark and latency tradeoffs, happy to jump in when we discuss quantization and batching.
00:36 Priya Menon: Great. main goals from our side: keep latency under 150ms p90 for customer-facing flows, not double our current costs, and get EU region for data residency. we also want an option to do private serving for most sensitive calls.
00:54 Alyssa Chen: Understood. on capacity, you mentioned a 20–30% uplift in email earlier, what are you thinking for committed vs burst?
01:06 Dana Ortega: We're leaning to a committed uplift ~25% with burstable headroom. procurement wants committed to justify budgeting.
01:14 Samir Patel: And contract term — we can do 12 months on green, we prefer not to lock to multi-year without seeing benchmarks.
01:22 Alyssa Chen: That's reasonable. we can draft a 12-month amendment with the 25% uplift and a burst policy. we'll include a pricing band for dedicated vs hosted.
01:33 Eileen Cho: For EU, we have two concerns: data residency and cross-region failover — so we need VPC connectivity and audit logs accessible to our SIEM.
01:45 Jules Park: We have a Private (VPC) option and Dedicated clusters. Private gives you customer-managed network and KMS control. Dedicated is faster to provision but with Redwood-managed networking.
01:59 Priya Menon: Can you confirm KMS/HSM options? Compliance wants encryption keys under our KMS if possible.
02:06 Marco Ruiz: Short answer: yes for Private. for Dedicated, we offer an integration with customer KMS for secrets and a sealed-key flow, but full HSM-backed brings some additional engineering — we can map that out.
02:20 Dana Ortega: OK, can you put that in writing and include any latency implications?
02:26 Marco Ruiz: Absolutely. a quick note — if you push keys to your KMS and use Private VPC, network egress is local so latency to EU region will be minimal; the bigger latency drivers are batch sizes and sequence lengths.
02:39 Priya Menon: Let's talk numbers — we currently run at 120ms p90 on our smaller model in US region at 100rps. we need predictions for EU: similar SLA.
02:50 Marco Ruiz: For EU we typically see similar p90 if we provision Dedicated with the same GPU profile. If you use aggressive batching to save cost you'll see higher variance. quantization (8-bit) helps throughput but might add a few ms and needs an eval to ensure quality doesn't regress.
03:06 Eileen Cho: How do fallbacks work? if the EU cluster is saturated do we failover to US? that's a legal problem for some EU data.
03:14 Jules Park: We support routing policies by data label; for EU-only traffic you can set strict routing so it never crosses the border. for non-sensitive you can set cost-first. fallback policies can be tailored per route.
03:28 Samir Patel: Procurement will want a clause about guaranteed locality for certain datasets. do you have audit logs retention options?
03:36 Jules Park: Yes, audit logs (API + admin) can be exported to your SIEM or S3. retention is configurable per contract; we can include 1yr default and extend if needed.
03:46 Dana Ortega: Great. pricing — give us a hosted vs dedicated delta and an option for a private pilot.
03:52 Alyssa Chen: we'll send a pricing pack: hosted per-token + region surcharge, dedicated fixed node pricing with a per-token overlay, and a private pilot hourly+setup fee. i'll include a scenario with the 25% uplift.
04:06 Priya Menon: For the pilot, we want a 48-hour benchmark using our traffic traces, plus an uplift test to simulate Black Friday-style peak.
04:15 Marco Ruiz: Plan sounds good. Proposed: 48-hr run, 200rps steady with 10-minute spikes to 1k for stress, collect p50/p90/p99, costs, and KV cache hit rates. will instrument tracing and token-level cost breakdown.
04:31 Eileen Cho: We'll share traffic CSVs and test keys. do you need us to whitelist IPs?
04:37 Marco Ruiz: For Private pilot, yes. For hosted we usually do a secure token. we'll send whitelisting instructions.
04:44 Dana Ortega: Security docs — SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, and any FedRAMP-related Qs — send them over please.
04:51 Jules Park: We'll attach the security pack. note: we have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and SSO via SAML + SCIM for provisioning. KMS integration note will be included.
04:59 Samir Patel: Legal will look at the amendment. timeline — if we get the docs and benchmark by mid-June, procurement can sign by end of month.
05:09 Alyssa Chen: Sounds good. let me recap: we'll deliver pricing + amendment draft (Alyssa), security pack (Jules), and a benchmark plan (Marco). Crestwood to provide traffic files and confirm the 25% uplift sign-off.
05:22 Priya Menon: Quick technical question — what about quantized model variants? we have concerns about hallucination rates dropping differently between FP16 and 8-bit quant.
05:32 Marco Ruiz: we'll include recommended quantization profiles by workload: low-latency chat vs high-quality summarization. and we'll tie quality checks to your eval harness so we can measure regressions.
05:45 Eileen Cho: If Dedicated provisioning is chosen, what's the lead time for EU nodes?
05:50 Alyssa Chen: Typical lead time for Dedicated EU nodes is 2–3 weeks from PO, Private VPC takes around 3–4 weeks depending on network reviews and firewall whitelisting. we'll note prioritization if you want a faster SLA as part of the amendment.
06:08 Dana Ortega: One wrinkle — our compliance team may require data residency for logs too. does Private give us full control?
06:16 Jules Park: Private gives you the control to route logs to your S3 in-region and you can manage retention. we'll include the step-by-step in the pack.
06:26 Samir Patel: On billing, can we get monthly invoicing and a committed usage credit applied monthly?
06:33 Alyssa Chen: Yes, invoicing monthly is standard. committed credits can be amortized monthly — we'll show an example amortization in the pricing scenarios.
06:42 Priya Menon: Anything on network egress costs when we add EU? need to understand total cost of ownership.
06:49 Marco Ruiz: We'll show egress assumptions and bring worst-case numbers. usually intra-cloud egress varies by provider; we'll make sure we model both.
06:58 Dana Ortega: Ok let's move to final decisions; we're comfortable to proceed with a 12-month amendment with 25% uplift pending benchmark results and security review.
07:08 Alyssa Chen: great. so action: sign off internally on the uplift, share traffic files, we'll run the benchmark, deliver the security pack and the amendment.
07:17 Eileen Cho: i'll get the traffic csv and a checklist for the networking team.
07:22 Samir Patel: procurement will target 2027-06-30 for signature if all goes well.
07:28 Alyssa Chen: Perfect. any other questions?
07:32 Priya Menon: one last ask — include a rollback/fallback playbook in case of quality regressions after rollout.
07:38 Marco Ruiz: we'll include rollback steps and an automatic fallback policy to a compatible model variant if you opt in.
07:45 Dana Ortega: Thanks everyone. that was productive.
07:49 Alyssa Chen: Thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and the DRAFT amendment.
07:53 Jules Park: i'll upload the security pack and SAML guide to the shared drive and link in the follow-up note.
07:58 Meeting close: ~58 minutes

Notes: Transcript contains small speaker label errors and occasional transcription artifacts. references to Redwoods products were transcribed variably (Private, Dedicated, VPC, KV cache).
